question.text: An organic compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> gives dark green colouration with ferric chloride. On treatment with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CHCl</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>KOH</mi><mo>,</mo></math> followed by acidification gives compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> can also be obtained from compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> on reaction with pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC). Identify <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text: The reaction with ferric chloride is test for phenol. The reaction of A with CHCl3 and KOH to give B is Riemer-Tiemann reaction. The conversion C to B is an oxidation reaction.
